headline: The DB's validated CQC coverage stops at the 2026-09-09 directory (checksum cf2e7bc2...). A newer 2026-09-16 directory (checksum bed9e95a..., 57,127 locations) exists and has NOT been ingested by any reconciliation batch. Against that newer source the DB holds 127 ACTIVE rows CQC no longer lists, of which 67 are confirmed DEREGISTERED by live CQC while still served as ACTIVE.

coverage_gap.statement: The newest source available is 2026-09-16 (sha256 bed9e95a1701, 57127 location ids). The newest snapshot the DB has actually validated is 2026-09-09 (sha256 cf2e7bc20493, 57151 locations) via batch b84cb3de-f70f-4d62-b5b3-639b09ceeffe completed 2026-09-16T12:00:07.325481+00:00. No reconciliation_batches row references the 2026-09-16 checksum, so the DB is one weekly publication behind.

db.query: SELECT status, count(*) FROM care_providers GROUP BY status

evidence: CQC directory CSV carries TWO identifier columns: 'CQC Location ID (for office use only)' (57,127 unique values, one per row) and 'CQC Provider ID (for office use only)' (37,088 unique values across 57,127 rows).
care_providers.id (PK, varchar(20)) intersects the CSV LOCATION ID column on 57,127/57,127 values (100%); it intersects the CSV PROVIDER ID column on 0 values.

care_providers.provider_id holds 38,024 non-NULL values of which 37,085 match CSV PROVIDER IDs and 0 match CSV LOCATION IDs -> provider_id is the parent-organisation reference (nullable, many locations per provider).
57,066 intersecting rows are DB ACTIVE and 61 are DB INACTIVE; there are 37,088 distinct providers vs 59,030 DB rows (~1.6 locations per provider) -> one DB row per CQC LOCATION, not per provider.

1,831 DB ids (1,774 ACTIVE + 57 INACTIVE) use CQC's legacy short location-id form (e.g. 'RHAR1', 'RP102'); 1,769 such short ids appear in the CSV location-id column. The `1-XXXXXXXXXXX` shape named in the task describes 57,199 of 59,030 DB rows and 55,358 of 57,127 snapshot rows; it is the modern CQC location-id shape, not a provider-id shape.
entity_type.conclusion: care_providers stores CQC LOCATIONS (one row per location). The table name is misleading; provider_id is the parent provider key.

notes: Read-only: SELECTs only; no DB writes of any kind, no commits, no repo edits.

1) curl -sS -A "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)" -o cqc_directory_2026-09-16.csv "https://www.cqc.org.uk/system/files/2026-09/16_september_2026_CQC_directory.csv" && shasum -a 256 cqc_directory_2026-09-16.csv
2) cd /Users/user/CareGist && ./.venv/bin/python <csv parse> -> 57,127 unique location ids; sha256 recomputed = bed9e95a1701ade0c4933bdf3acda7a9c4c94e3940a19ad698575a05a66eecb0
3) SELECT id, status FROM care_providers  (59,030 rows) compared as Python sets against the snapshot id set
4) GET {DEFAULT_BASE_URL}/locations/{id} for all 188 divergent ids (127 only_in_db_active + 61 source_but_db_inactive)
Entity-type evidence is identifier-based (CSV Location ID vs Provider ID columns crossed against care_providers.id and provider_id); it does not rest on the table name.
only_in_source is 0: every id in the 2026-09-16 snapshot already has a care_providers row, so the divergence is entirely status-side plus 127 DB-only ACTIVE rows.
1,769 of the 57,127 snapshot rows use CQC's legacy short location-id form and were matched as-is; no id normalisation was applied.
